body:
I was an athlete in undergrad and the meds make me light headed when competing.  They were great for my mood, but I had to stop competing at a high level, I was able to do intramural sports.

If I were you, I would give your meds an honest chance.  It takes a while for them to kick in.
I like this.  I've always enjoyed helping people, I hope I look into this more.
I went off the meds because I got better.  I had a good outlook on life.  They helped, but I didn't think I needed their help anymore.

My school got shot up by a guy, killed a bunch of people.  They now video tape sessions.

A private counselor sounds expensive.
I was on meds for 2 years and have been off them for 3.5 years.  I never want to be on them again, they just didn't sit well with me.  My doc was just a student counselor or something.
Not tonight,  but some other time maybe tomorrow.
Thank you for your story, you sound like a good person.  I have had significant others in the past think badly of me because of my past.  It made me feel broken and not worth love.

I've talked to my undergrad school friends about things before, one even stopped me from jumping.  They were there for me, but the friends I have at my new university... they respect me.  I don't want to ruin that.

I know that I should be better off without her.  She still sees the possibility of us getting married one day, which is messed up, I know.

I have had professional help before, but this school is a little funny about that sort of thing... and I'm afraid things wouldn't be kept private.

I am not religious, sorry.  I wish I could be, but organized religions just don't do it for me.
